key-cutting.q: How much does it cost to get a key cut in Australia?
key-cutting.a: A basic house key cut commonly costs $5 to $15 at a hardware store or mobile locksmith, while car and transponder keys start around $80 and can exceed $350 for luxury or smart-key models. Price depends on key type, blank availability and whether programming is required.

key-cutting.q: Why do car keys cost more than house keys?
key-cutting.a: Car keys often contain a transponder chip that must be cut and electronically programmed to the vehicle's immobiliser, requiring specialised equipment locksmiths pay to license. A house key is a simple metal cut, while a programmed car key involves diagnostics, software and matching security codes.

key-cutting.q: Can a mobile locksmith cut keys on the spot?
key-cutting.a: Most mobile locksmiths carry blanks for common house and older car keys and can cut them on site within minutes. Modern transponder or smart keys sometimes need parts ordered in advance, so it is worth confirming your key type and vehicle when booking to avoid a return visit.

lock-rekeying.q: How much does lock rekeying cost in Australia?
lock-rekeying.a: Rekeying a standard residential lock typically costs $60 to $150 per lock, with whole-house jobs of four to six locks often priced $250 to $600. Cost depends on lock brand, number of cylinders and whether the locksmith charges a callout fee.

lock-rekeying.q: What is the difference between rekeying and replacing a lock?
lock-rekeying.a: Rekeying changes the internal pins so old keys no longer work while keeping the existing hardware, making it cheaper and faster than replacement. Lock replacement swaps the entire mechanism and is needed when a lock is damaged, outdated or you want a different style or higher security rating.

lock-rekeying.q: When should I rekey instead of replace my locks?
lock-rekeying.a: Rekeying suits situations like moving into a new home, losing keys, or after a tenant leaves, where the lock itself is still in good condition. If the lock is worn, damaged or you want upgraded security features, full replacement is the better long-term option despite the higher cost.

emergency-lockout-service.q: How much does an emergency lockout service cost in Australia?
emergency-lockout-service.a: Emergency lockouts commonly cost $100 to $250 during business hours, rising to $150 to $350 for after-hours, night or weekend callouts. Final price depends on lock type, entry difficulty and how far the locksmith has to travel to reach you.

emergency-lockout-service.q: How fast can a locksmith respond to a lockout?
emergency-lockout-service.a: Most urban locksmiths aim to arrive within 30 to 60 minutes for emergency lockouts, though response times stretch longer in regional areas or during peak demand periods like storms. Confirming your location and lock type upfront helps the locksmith prepare and arrive faster.

emergency-lockout-service.q: Will I need a new lock after being locked out?
emergency-lockout-service.a: Most lockouts are resolved with non-destructive entry techniques that leave your existing lock intact and reusable. A replacement is only needed if the lock is damaged during entry, was already faulty, or the key has broken off inside the cylinder and cannot be extracted.

lock-change-and-replacement.q: How much does it cost to change or replace a lock in Australia?
lock-change-and-replacement.a: Replacing a standard door lock typically costs $150 to $400 including the new hardware and labour, while higher-security or smart locks can run $400 to $800 or more. Price varies with lock brand, door type and how many locks need replacing.

lock-change-and-replacement.q: How long does a lock replacement take?
lock-change-and-replacement.a: A standard single lock replacement usually takes 30 to 60 minutes once the locksmith is on site, assuming the door is in good condition and a matching strike plate is already fitted. Multiple locks or doors needing carpentry adjustments will take longer.

lock-change-and-replacement.q: Should I upgrade to a higher security lock when replacing?
lock-change-and-replacement.a: Many homeowners use a replacement as an opportunity to upgrade from a basic pin-tumbler lock to a higher security or deadlatch option, which costs more upfront but resists picking and drilling better. It is worth discussing insurance requirements with your locksmith before choosing.

digital-lock-installation.q: How much does digital lock installation cost in Australia?
digital-lock-installation.a: Digital and smart lock installation commonly costs $350 to $900 including the unit and fitting, with premium biometric or app-connected models pushing towards $1,200 or more. Cost depends on the lock brand, door compatibility and whether existing hardware needs modification.

digital-lock-installation.q: Do digital locks work during a power outage?
digital-lock-installation.a: Most residential digital locks run on standard batteries rather than mains power, so they continue working through outages, though batteries typically need replacing every six to twelve months. Many models also include a physical key override as a backup entry method.

digital-lock-installation.q: Can a digital lock be fitted to any door?
digital-lock-installation.a: Digital locks generally fit standard timber and aluminium doors with minor modification, but older or non-standard door types may need extra prep work or a compatible strike plate. A locksmith can assess your door during a quote before confirming the final installation price.

hoarder-clean-up.q: How much does a hoarder clean-up cost in Australia?
hoarder-clean-up.a: Hoarder clean-ups commonly range from $1,000 to $10,000 or more, driven mainly by the volume of items, number of skip bins needed and whether biohazard materials are present. Small single-room jobs sit at the lower end, while whole-property clean-ups with heavy contamination cost significantly more.

hoarder-clean-up.q: What is included in a hoarder clean-up service?
hoarder-clean-up.a: A typical service includes sorting items for keep, donate or dispose, removal and skip bin hire, and a deep clean of the space once it is cleared. Some jobs also include odour treatment, pest control referral and coordination with family or support services throughout the process.

hoarder-clean-up.q: How long does a hoarder clean-up take?
hoarder-clean-up.a: A single room can often be cleared in a day, while a full house clean-up commonly takes two to five days depending on volume, access and whether sorting decisions need family involvement. Severely affected properties with structural or biohazard issues can take longer to complete safely.

hoarder-house-clean-up.q: How much does a hoarder house clean-up cost in Australia?
hoarder-house-clean-up.a: A full hoarder house clean-up typically costs $2,000 to $10,000 or more, scaling with the number of rooms, item volume and whether biohazard or structural cleaning is required. Multi-storey homes and properties with vehicle access issues generally sit at the higher end.

hoarder-house-clean-up.q: Do hoarder house clean-ups include rubbish removal?
hoarder-house-clean-up.a: Yes, rubbish and unwanted item removal is a core part of the service, usually priced into the quote alongside skip bin hire and tip fees. Larger properties may require multiple skip bins or truck loads, which is factored into the overall cost upfront.

hoarder-house-clean-up.q: Can a hoarder house clean-up be done sensitively for the occupant?
hoarder-house-clean-up.a: Reputable clean-up teams work at a pace that respects the occupant, involving them in sorting decisions where possible rather than discarding items without consent. Many operators also coordinate with family members or support workers to make the process less overwhelming for everyone involved.

tree-removal.q: How much does tree removal cost in Australia?
tree-removal.a: Tree removal commonly costs $500 to $5,000 or more, depending mainly on tree height, trunk diameter, access for equipment and proximity to structures or power lines. Small trees in open yards sit at the lower end, while large trees needing crane access cost significantly more.

tree-removal.q: Do I need council approval to remove a tree?
tree-removal.a: Many councils require a permit to remove significant or protected trees, and rules vary widely by council and by whether the tree is native, heritage-listed or over a certain size. Always check with your local council before removal, as unauthorised removal of a protected tree can carry penalties.

tree-removal.q: What factors affect the price of tree removal?
tree-removal.a: Price is driven by tree size, trunk diameter, how difficult the site is to access, and whether branches must be removed near a house, fence or powerlines. Stump removal, wood disposal and whether a crane or crane truck is needed all add to the final quoted price.

stump-grinding.q: How much does stump grinding cost in Australia?
stump-grinding.a: Stump grinding commonly costs $100 to $400 per stump, depending on trunk diameter, root spread and how accessible the stump is for grinding equipment. Multiple stumps on one job often attract a discounted per-stump rate compared to a single callout.

stump-grinding.q: Is stump grinding better than digging a stump out?
stump-grinding.a: Stump grinding is usually faster and cheaper than digging a stump out by hand or excavator, since it grinds the wood down below ground level without disturbing surrounding soil or nearby structures. Full excavation is generally only needed when all roots must be removed for new construction.

stump-grinding.q: How deep does stump grinding go?
stump-grinding.a: Standard stump grinding typically removes the stump 15 to 30 centimetres below ground level, which is enough for replanting grass or garden beds over the area. Deeper grinding is available for an extra cost if you plan to build or lay hard surfacing over the site.

tree-lopping.q: How much does tree lopping cost in Australia?
tree-lopping.a: Tree lopping commonly costs $300 to $2,500 depending on tree size, how much canopy is being removed and site access for equipment. Larger trees or jobs requiring traffic control and elevated work platforms sit toward the higher end of that range.

tree-lopping.q: Is tree lopping the same as pruning?
tree-lopping.a: Lopping involves cutting back large sections of a tree, often to reduce height or clear powerlines, while pruning is more selective, removing smaller branches to improve shape and health. Many arborists now recommend pruning over heavy lopping because it causes less stress to the tree.

tree-lopping.q: Does tree lopping require council approval?
tree-lopping.a: Many councils require a permit for significant lopping work, particularly on protected, native or heritage-listed trees, and rules vary widely by council. It is worth checking local requirements before booking, since unauthorised lopping of a protected tree can carry financial penalties.

emergency-tree-removal.q: How much does emergency tree removal cost in Australia?
emergency-tree-removal.a: Emergency tree removal, such as after storm damage, commonly costs $800 to $6,000 or more, reflecting after-hours callout fees, urgency and the complexity of removing a fallen or unstable tree safely. Trees resting on structures or powerlines cost more due to the specialist equipment required.

emergency-tree-removal.q: How quickly can an emergency tree removal crew arrive?
emergency-tree-removal.a: Most emergency arborist services aim to respond within a few hours for genuinely dangerous situations, such as a tree blocking access or threatening a structure, though response times extend during widespread storm events when demand spikes sharply across an entire region.

emergency-tree-removal.q: What should I do before an emergency tree crew arrives?
emergency-tree-removal.a: Keep people and pets well clear of the affected area, especially if branches or powerlines are involved, and avoid attempting to move debris yourself. Photograph the damage for insurance purposes and contact your provider or emergency services first if there is any risk to safety.

termite-inspection.q: How much does a termite inspection cost in Australia?
termite-inspection.a: A standard termite inspection commonly costs $250 to $600, depending on property size, accessibility of subfloor and roof areas, and whether a written report is included. Larger or harder-to-access properties, such as those with extensive subfloor space, sit toward the higher end.

termite-inspection.q: Is a termite inspection required before buying a house?
termite-inspection.a: A termite inspection is strongly recommended before buying a house, even though it is not always legally required, since undetected termite damage can be costly to repair. Many buyers make their purchase conditional on a satisfactory pest and building report during the contract period.

termite-inspection.q: How often should a termite inspection be done?
termite-inspection.a: Most pest professionals recommend an annual termite inspection for Australian properties, or every six months in high-risk termite areas such as parts of Queensland and northern New South Wales. Regular inspections catch early activity before it causes significant structural damage.

termite-treatment.q: How much does termite treatment cost in Australia?
termite-treatment.a: Full termite treatment commonly costs $1,500 to $5,000, depending on property size, treatment method and whether a chemical soil barrier, baiting system or physical barrier is used. Ongoing monitoring and warranty plans are often priced separately on top of the initial treatment.

termite-treatment.q: What is included in professional termite treatment?
termite-treatment.a: Treatment typically includes an initial inspection, application of a chemical or baiting barrier around the property, and treatment of any active infestation found in timber or subfloor areas. Many providers also include a follow-up inspection and a warranty period as part of the package.

termite-treatment.q: How long does termite treatment last?
termite-treatment.a: Chemical soil barriers commonly last five to eight years before requiring reapplication, while baiting systems need ongoing monitoring and bait replacement every few months to remain effective. Your pest provider should specify the expected treatment life and warranty terms in writing.

cockroach-treatment.q: How much does cockroach treatment cost in Australia?
cockroach-treatment.a: Cockroach treatment for a standard home commonly costs $150 to $400, with larger properties, commercial kitchens or severe infestations pushing costs higher due to extra product and follow-up visits. Price also depends on whether internal and external treatment, or a full fumigation, is required.

cockroach-treatment.q: How long does it take to get rid of cockroaches?
cockroach-treatment.a: A single professional treatment often reduces visible activity within a few days, but fully breaking the breeding cycle typically takes two to four weeks, sometimes with a follow-up visit included. Severe infestations may need a second treatment for complete control.

cockroach-treatment.q: Is cockroach treatment safe for pets and children?
cockroach-treatment.a: Licensed pest technicians use products approved for residential use and apply them in ways designed to minimise exposure, such as targeted gel baits and treating areas away from food preparation. It is still common practice to keep pets and children away from treated areas until the product has dried or settled.
